# Light direction fixed in image space [S1, unofficial]

The evidence explicitly states in the notes and the main text that 'PixelFlow supports general lighting by sources fixed in image-space' and contrasts this with the RealityEngine's precomputed shading which 'fixes the light position(s) relative to the volume' (object space). The text confirms that PixelFlow achieves image-space lighting by using normalized data gradients instead of precomputed coefficients.

PixelFlow Volume Rendering is a polygon resampling method designed for the PixelFlow graphics system that overcomes the lighting and data size limitations of the RealityEngine by allowing pixel processors to manipulate 3D texture values directly [S1, unofficial].

The text explicitly states that PixelFlow is a 'variant of the polygon resampling approach' designed for the 'PixelFlow graphics system'. It confirms that this approach 'overcome[s] the limitations on realistic lighting and data size imposed by the RealityEngine'. Furthermore, the text explains that PixelFlow's texturing hardware allows '128^2 pixel processors' to access texture values which are then 'manipulated... as ordinary data' by user programs, directly supporting the claim about pixel processors manipulating 3D texture values directly.
